name: Naturewatch

targetAreaEffect.value: Quarter circle emanating from you to the extreme of the range

description: You cast this exactly as you would deathwatch, but the spell reads only animals and plants, not the full range of the living and dying. Within a quarter-circle radiating from you out to the spell's range, you sense how near each animal or plant is to death, the same information deathwatch shows for any creature. You also pick up on other everyday conditions as you look — whether a plant is dehydrated, an animal malnourished, and similar mundane details. Casting requires only a somatic gesture, no words, and the effect lasts 10 minutes per caster level.

name: Beget Bogun
description:
This is the final spell in creating a bogun: you infuse living magic into a small mannequin you've already woven from vegetable matter, the mannequin serving as the spell's material component. Casting costs 25 XP and takes effect instantly, with no saving throw or spell resistance to resist it.

The bogun that results is a Tiny construct with 2 Hit Dice (2d10, roughly 11 hp). Its ability scores are Str 7, Dex 16, Con —, Int 8, Wis 13, and Cha 10. It has AC 15, touch 15, flat-footed 12, with an initiative modifier of +3. It moves at a speed of 20 feet on the ground, or 50 feet flying with good maneuverability. It attacks with a nettle strike at +1 melee, dealing 1d4–2 points of damage plus poison. Its saves are Fort +0, Ref +3, Will +1. Its skills are Hide +10 and Move Silently +9, and it has the Stealthy feat. Its Challenge Rating is 1. It's always the same alignment as its creator. As a construct, it doesn't need to breathe, eat, or sleep, and it's immune to poison, disease, and mind-affecting effects.

A bogun shares your alignment and, much like a homunculus, remains an extension of you rather than a fully independent creature. It can't speak, but the ritual that creates it links it to you telepathically, and it relays everything it sees and hears back to you across a range of 500 yards. It never willingly travels beyond that range, and if it's forced beyond it, it spends all its effort trying to regain contact with you. It carries out whatever simple task you set it — attacking, delivering a message, opening an unlatched door or window — and it can perform any straightforward chore that doesn't call for an understanding of a mechanism. On any given task, though, there's a 5% chance it balks. When that happens, you must succeed on a DC 11 Diplomacy check to talk it into cooperating. If that check fails, the bogun either does the exact opposite of what you asked, or refuses to do anything at all for the next 24 hours, at the DM's discretion. If an attack destroys the bogun, you take 2d10 points of damage yourself. If you die, the bogun dies with you, and its body collapses into a heap of rotting vegetation.

name: Camouflage
description: You alter the coloring of your skin and clothing to match whatever surroundings you're in. As you move from one environment to another, your coloration shifts instantly to match the new background, with no effort or concentration required on your part. You gain a +10 circumstance bonus on Hide checks for as long as the spell lasts — 10 minutes per caster level.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the identical Masters of the Wild printing of the same spell, which does print these lines explicitly.

name: Hawkeye
description: Your eyes sharpen to pick out detail at long range. Your range increment with projectile weapons increases by 50% for the duration. You also gain a +5 competence bonus on all Spot checks. The effect lasts 10 minutes per caster level.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Omen of Peril
description:
You offer a brief supplication and receive a flash of foresight, lasting only a second or two, warning you how dangerous your immediate future looks. The base chance that your vision is accurate is 70% plus 1% per caster level, capping at 90%; the DM rolls this secretly, so you never know for certain whether you can trust what you see.

If the roll succeeds, you receive one of three visions. A vision of safety means you'll face no significant monsters, traps, or other threats for about the next hour if you continue on your present course, or stay where you are if you've been stationary. A vision of peril means you'll face the ordinary dangers of an adventure — challenging but not overwhelming monsters, hazardous traps, and other typical hazards. A vision of great danger means your life is at serious risk, and you're likely to run into powerful foes or deadly traps within the hour. If the roll fails, you instead receive one of the other two visions, chosen at random by the DM, and because the roll was secret, you have no way of knowing you were misled.

The exact form of the vision follows your faith. A druid, for example, might see a white dove for safety, a dark cloud swallowing the sun for peril, or a forest fire for great danger, while a cleric of a different deity would see something tied to that deity's own symbolism. Unlike the more powerful augury spell, omen of peril doesn't answer a specific question — it only tells you the general level of danger ahead, not what shape that danger will take. Casting it takes a full round, and you need a focus of marked sticks, bones, or similar tokens worth at least 25 gp.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Sandblast

targetAreaEffect.value: Semicircular burst of sand 10 ft. long, centered on your hands

description: You fire a hail of hot sand from your fingertips in a semicircular arc 10 feet long, centered on your hands. Everyone caught in the arc takes 1d6 points of nonlethal damage. Anyone who fails a Reflex save is also stunned for 1 round.

name: Traveler’s Mount
description: You touch an animal or magical beast and make it better suited to the rigors of overland travel, at the cost of its willingness to fight. The mount gains a +10-foot enhancement bonus to its speed for 1 hour per caster level. It can hustle for that whole duration without risking nonlethal damage or fatigue. In exchange, it stops using its natural weapons in combat — it still willingly carries its rider into the middle of a fight, it simply won't strike out with tooth, claw, or horn on its own. A Will save negates the effect if the mount resists it.

name: Vigor, Lesser
description: You touch a living creature and boost its life energy, granting it fast healing 1 for the duration of the spell. The subject heals 1 hit point of damage every round until the spell ends. If it begins dying from hit point loss while the spell is active, it's automatically stabilized. The healing doesn't restore hit points lost to starvation, thirst, or suffocation, and it won't regrow or reattach a lost body part. The spell lasts 10 rounds plus 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 15 rounds. Multiple vigor spells never stack on the same creature — only the strongest one currently active does anything — but casting a second vigor spell of the same level on a creature already under one extends the current duration by the new spell's full duration.

name: Wood Wose
description: You conjure a translucent, green nature spirit that carries out simple natural chores at your direction. It can build a campfire, gather herbs, feed your animal companion, catch a fish, or handle any other basic task that doesn't call for an understanding of technology — it can't, for instance, work a latch to open a chest. The wose performs one activity at a time, and if you tell it to keep doing something, it repeats that task on its own while your attention is elsewhere, as long as you stay within range. Its effective Strength score is only 2, so it can lift 20 pounds or drag 100 pounds; it's strong enough to trigger a trap, but not strong enough to set off most pressure plates. It moves 15 feet per round in any direction, including straight up. It can never attack, and it's never subject to an attack roll or a saving throw. Six points of damage from an area attack dissipates it entirely, and if you try to send it beyond the spell's range measured from your current position, it simply ceases to exist. The spell lasts 1 hour per caster level.

name: Body of the Sun
description: You draw on the power of the sun and wrap your body in fire for 1 round per caster level. The flame extends 5 feet from you in every direction, so it lights up the area around you. Any creature other than you that the fire touches takes 1d4+1 points of fire damage, or half that on a successful Reflex save.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry omits dedicated Saving Throw and Spell Resistance lines entirely (confirmed against the source PDF, page 155) — an apparent editorial oversight, not a formatting choice specific to this spell. Saving Throw is inferred from the description's own 'Reflex save for half' wording; Spell Resistance is inferred as Yes per standard 3.5e convention for an energy-damage spell affecting other creatures, since the book states no exception.

name: Brambles
description: You touch a wooden weapon — a club, greatclub, nunchaku, quarterstaff, or similar melee weapon with a wooden striking surface — and cause small magical thorns and spikes to sprout across it. For 1 round per caster level, the weapon deals piercing damage in addition to its normal bludgeoning damage. It also gains a +1 enhancement bonus on attack rolls made with it. It deals an extra point of damage per caster level, to a maximum of +10. The spell only works on melee weapons with a wooden striking surface — it has no effect on a bow, an arrow, or a metal-headed weapon like a mace. You need a small thorn as a material component.

name: Briar Web
description:
You cause the grasses, weeds, bushes, and even trees within a 20-foot-radius spread to grow thorns, and the plants reach out to snare anyone in or entering the area for 1 minute per caster level. A creature that makes its saving throw is only slowed to half speed while it's in the area — the thorns don't grab hold of it.

A creature that fails its save has three choices each round it remains inside the area. It can hold perfectly still, in which case it becomes entangled, taking a –2 penalty on attack rolls and a –4 penalty to effective Dexterity, but suffers no other harm, and the entangled condition ends the moment it leaves the area. It can spend a full-round action trying to break free, which grants it a new saving throw; success frees it from the thorns, though it's still limited to half speed while inside the area, while failure deals the normal 2d6 points of piercing damage. Or it can simply act — attacking, casting a spell with a somatic component, or moving normally — in which case it takes that same 2d6 points of piercing damage from the thorns, and if it was casting a spell, it must also succeed on a Concentration check, with a DC of 15 plus the spell's level plus the damage just taken, or lose the spell entirely. The tangled plants also provide cover: a creature 5 feet away has cover, and creatures separated by 20 feet or more of briar web have total cover from each other.

name: Cloudburst
description: You cause storm clouds to gather and a heavy rain to fall across a 100-foot-radius emanation for 10 minutes per caster level. The downpour cuts visibility in half, giving a –4 penalty on Spot and Search checks. It imposes a –4 penalty on ranged weapon attacks and on Listen checks. It automatically extinguishes any unprotected flame, and it has a 50% chance of extinguishing a protected one. The spell doesn't function indoors, underground, underwater, or in desert climates. Once the spell ends, the water it created evaporates over the next 10 minutes, and at no point does it slake anyone's thirst or nourish any plant.

otherPrintings.note: Same name, unrelated spell — different school/mechanics, not a reprint

name: Creeping Cold
description: You turn the sweat on the subject's body to ice, raising painful blisters as it forms on and beneath the skin. The spell deals 1d6 points of cold damage on the first round, 2d6 points on the second, and 3d6 points on the third, for 3 rounds total. Only one Fortitude save is allowed, made the instant the spell is cast; if it succeeds, the damage in every round is halved instead of negated. You need a small glass or pottery vessel worth at least 25 gp, filled with ice, snow, or water, as a focus.

name: Decomposition

targetAreaEffect.value: All enemies within a 50-ft.-radius emanation cen- tered on you

description: You curse every enemy within a 50-foot emanation centered on you so that their wounds fester instead of healing normally. Whenever an affected enemy takes normal damage — not subdual damage — that wound continues to bleed for 1 additional point of damage every round afterward, for 1 round per caster level. Only one wound festers on a given creature at a time; if it takes more damage while the first wound is still festering, the new damage doesn't start its own festering. A successful DC 15 Heal check, or any curative magic such as a cure spell, heal, or healing circle, stops the current festering. If the creature suffers a fresh wound while it's still inside the area and the spell hasn't expired yet, the festering begins again from that new wound.

name: Scent
description: You touch a creature and give it an enhanced sense of smell, equal to the scent ability that many monsters have, for 10 minutes per caster level. It can detect an approaching opponent within 30 feet; that range extends to 60 feet if the opponent is upwind, or shrinks to 15 feet if downwind. A strong odor, such as smoke or rotting garbage, doubles these ranges, and an overpowering one, such as skunk musk or troglodyte stench, triples them. Detecting a scent this way only reveals that something is present somewhere within range — the creature can spend a partial action to work out the direction, and closing to within 5 feet pinpoints the source exactly. It can also follow a trail by smell with a Wisdom check, using a base DC of 10 for a fresh trail regardless of the surface, increasing by 2 for every hour the trail has cooled, and following the same rules as the Track feat; tracking this way ignores the usual penalties from poor surface conditions or bad visibility. Casting requires a sprinkle of mustard and pepper and a drop of sweat as an arcane material component.

name: Beast Claws
description: Your fingers lengthen into long, curved claws over heavy knuckles for 1 round per caster level. The claws work as slashing melee weapons that deal 1d6 points of damage, plus any bonus you'd normally add from Strength or magic, with a threat range of 19–20. Attacking with them doesn't provoke an attack of opportunity. They don't interfere with your manual dexterity or your ability to cast spells. You need the claw of a bird of prey, such as an eagle or falcon, as a material component.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Fire Wings
description:
Your arms transform into wings of brilliant fire for 1 minute per caster level. The flame doesn't harm you or anything you're carrying. Because your arms have become wings, you can't hold anything in your hands or cast a spell with a somatic component while the wings are active, though rings, bracers, and other items you're already wearing on your arms keep working normally. The wings let you fly at a speed of 60 feet, or 40 feet if you're wearing medium or heavy armor, with good maneuverability. You can charge while flying, but you can't run, and you can't carry more than a light load aloft. Flying this way takes no more concentration than walking, so you're free to take other actions as normal.

If the spell's duration runs out while you're still aloft, you descend at 60 feet per round for 1d6 rounds and then fall the rest of the way if you haven't landed by then; the same controlled descent happens if the spell is dispelled, though not if it's suppressed by an antimagic field instead. You can also strike with the wings as unarmed attacks, though you fight at a –4 penalty since you're not proficient with them; a successful hit deals 2d6 points of fire damage on top of your normal unarmed damage. A quench spell, full immersion in water, or a wind of hurricane force or stronger puts the wings out and ends the spell. You need a bird's feather as a material component, which you burn as you cast the spell, plus a golden amulet shaped like a phoenix as a focus.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Infestation of Maggots
description: You make a melee touch attack, and if it hits, you infest the target with maggotlike creatures that burrow beneath its skin. They deal 1d4 points of temporary Constitution damage every round for 1 round per 2 caster levels. Each round, the subject can attempt a new Fortitude save to negate that round's damage and end the infestation early. A cure disease spell or a heal spell also removes it. You need a handful of dead, dried flies as a material component.

name: Nature’s Favor
description: You touch an animal and call on nature's own favor to bless it. The animal gains a +1 luck bonus on attack and damage rolls for every 2 caster levels you have. The bonus lasts 1 minute per caster level. A Will save negates the effect if it resists, though the effect is harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way.

name: Spikes
description: This spell works exactly like brambles, except the enchantment is sturdier: the wooden weapon instead gains a +2 enhancement bonus on its attack rolls, and its threat range is doubled. The effect lasts 1 hour per caster level.

name: Standing Wave

targetAreaEffect.value: Waves under a creature or object within range

description: You command the water beneath a creature or object within range to rise up and carry it forward. An object lifted this way may itself be carrying other creatures or objects. How large a creature or object the wave can lift depends on your caster level. At 5th level, it can lift anything up to Medium size. At 7th level, it can lift a Large creature or object. At 9th level, Huge. At 11th level, Gargantuan. At 13th level or higher, Colossal. Once lifted, the standing wave carries its burden in a straight line across the water's surface at a speed of 60 feet per round. The spell ends the moment the wave reaches land, and its burden is lowered gently to the shore. A Reflex save negates the effect, and spell resistance applies.

name: Vigor
description: This spell works exactly like lesser vigor, except it grants fast healing 2 instead of fast healing 1. It lasts 10 rounds plus 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 25 rounds.

name: Vigor, Mass Lesser

targetAreaEffect.value: One creature/two levels, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

description: You extend lesser vigor's healing across a group instead of a single creature. You grant fast healing 1 to one creature per two caster levels, no two of which can be more than 30 feet apart. Each subject heals 1 hit point every round until the spell ends. If a subject begins dying from hit point loss while the spell is active, it's automatically stabilized. As with lesser vigor, the healing doesn't restore hit points lost to starvation, thirst, or suffocation, and it won't regrow or reattach a lost body part. It lasts 10 rounds plus 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 25 rounds. Multiple vigor spells still don't stack — only the strongest one active on a creature does anything — though a second vigor spell of the same level extends the current duration by its own full duration.

name: Weather Eye

targetAreaEffect.value: 1 mile radius + 1 mile/level, centered on you

description: You spend a full hour in divination and afterward can accurately predict the natural weather up to a week into the future, across an area with a radius of 1 mile plus 1 mile per caster level, centered on you. If unnatural forces are currently affecting the weather in that area, the spell instead reveals as much about that influence as a detect magic spell would. You need a stick of incense as a material component and a scrying device — a bowl, mirror, or crystal ball, for instance — as a divine focus.

name: Bottle of Smoke
description:
You use a source of fire to draw a plume of smoke into a specially prepared bottle you're holding. If you open the bottle before the spell's duration runs out, the smoke emerges and takes the form of a vaguely horselike creature. It makes no sound, and anything that touches it simply passes through.

To mount the smoke horse, a rider must hold the bottle in one hand and succeed on a DC 10 Ride check. Anyone who tries to mount without holding the bottle just passes through the horse's form instead. If the rider lets go of the bottle after mounting, they fall through the horse and can't remount until they're holding the intact bottle again. If the bottle breaks, the spell ends immediately, and any mounted rider falls to the ground.

The smoke horse moves at 20 feet per caster level, to a maximum of 240 feet. At the rider's command, it can trail smoke billowing out behind it, leaving a bank of smoke 5 feet wide and 20 feet high as it moves; starting or stopping the trail is a free action. A wind of at least 31 miles per hour, or any magical wind, disperses the horse and any smoke it has laid down instantly; otherwise, the smoke bank lasts 10 minutes from when it's laid down. The mount and its smoke trail grant one-half concealment, a 20% miss chance, to anyone using them for cover. The mount can't be harmed, since weapons and spells simply pass through it, and it can't attack.

The rider can return the horse to the bottle at any time, pausing the spell: this takes a move-equivalent action to uncork the bottle, and once the horse is back inside, another move-equivalent action the following round to stopper it again. Reopening the bottle later resumes the spell with whatever duration remained. No matter how much of that duration goes unused, the spell stops working entirely 24 hours after you first cast it, and dispelling it while the bottle is corked ends it right away. You need an ornate, corked bottle worth at least 50 gp as a focus.

name: Camouflage, Mass

targetAreaEffect.value: Any number of creatures, no two of which can be more than 60 ft. apart

description: This spell works like camouflage, except the effect covers a whole group and moves with them. You can affect any number of creatures, provided no two of them are ever more than 60 feet apart, for 10 minutes per caster level. If any individual moves more than 60 feet from the nearest other member of the group, the spell breaks for that person alone. If only two creatures are affected and one moves away from the other, only the one moving away loses the camouflage. If both of them move apart from each other at once, they both lose it the moment the distance between them exceeds 60 feet.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the identical Masters of the Wild printing of the same spell, which does print these lines explicitly.

name: Chain of Eyes
description: You touch a living creature and gain the ability to see through its eyes instead of your own, for 1 hour per caster level. The spell gives you no control over the creature's actions. Whenever the linked creature comes into physical contact with another living being, you can choose to shift your sensor to that new creature instead, letting you follow a chain of contact into a place you couldn't otherwise reach. On your turn, you can switch, as a free action, between seeing through the linked creature's eyes and seeing normally, and back again. A Will save negates the effect, and spell resistance applies.

name: Energy Vortex
description: When you cast this spell, you choose one energy type: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. A blast of that energy bursts outward from your body in every direction, striking every other creature within a 20-foot burst centered on you. It deals 1d8 points of damage plus 1 point per caster level, to a maximum of +20. If you're willing to take the damage yourself, you can deal double damage instead, though you take your own share of it too. There's no Reflex save against the blast, but spell resistance still applies, and so do any resistances or immunities the target has to that energy type.

name: Forestfold
description: This spell works like camouflage, but the effect is sharper: instead of shifting your coloration, it grants you a +20 competence bonus on Hide checks and a +20 competence bonus on Move Silently checks. The spell ends immediately if you move more than 10 feet from the spot where you cast it.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the identical Masters of the Wild printing of the same spell, which does print these lines explicitly.

name: Languor
description: You fire a ray at a target, and if it hits and the target fails a Will save, it becomes weak and slow. The target is slowed, exactly as the slow spell affects it. Each round the effect continues, the target also takes a cumulative enhancement penalty to Strength equal to 1d6–1 for every two caster levels you have, with a minimum additional penalty of 0 per round and a maximum total penalty of –10. If the target's Strength score drops below 1, it becomes helpless. The slow effect is countered by haste and counters it in turn, but haste has no effect on the accumulating Strength penalty. The spell lasts 1 round per caster level.

name: Last Breath
description:
You touch a creature that died within the last round and return it to 0 hit points. Doing so costs you 1d4 points of damage per Hit Die the creature has, and your own spell resistance can't stop this damage. The subject's soul must be free and willing to return, following the normal rules for bringing back the dead. If the soul isn't willing, the spell simply fails, and because of that, a willing subject gets no saving throw either way.

Last breath heals the subject enough to bring it to exactly 0 hit points. It raises any ability score that was reduced to 0 or below back up to 1. It cures ordinary poison and ordinary disease, though it has no effect on magical diseases or curses. It closes mortal wounds and repairs most lethal damage, but any body part the creature was missing when it died is still missing when it returns, and none of its equipment or possessions are affected in any way.

Coming back exacts its usual price: the subject loses one level, exactly as if an energy-draining creature had drained it, and no spell can undo that loss. If the subject was only 1st level, it loses 1 point of Constitution instead. A character who died with spells prepared has a 50% chance, checked separately for each prepared spell, of losing that spell on top of what's lost to the level drain. A spontaneous caster who didn't prepare spells instead has a 50% chance, checked separately for each unused spell slot, of losing that slot the same way. The spell has no effect on a creature that has been dead for more than 1 round. It can't restore a creature killed by a death effect, and it can't affect a construct, an elemental, an outsider, or an undead creature. It also can't bring back someone who died of old age.

name: Murderous Mist

targetAreaEffect.value: Cloud that spreads in 30-ft. radius, 20 ft. high

description: You create a cloud of scalding steam that spreads out to a 30-foot radius and 20 feet high, then moves in a straight line away from you at 10 feet per round for 1 round per caster level. Anyone inside the cloud takes 2d6 points of damage and is permanently blinded. A creature that succeeds on a Reflex save instead takes only half damage and isn't blinded. Anyone inside the cloud has one-quarter concealment. Ordinary wind doesn't change the cloud's direction or speed, but a moderate wind of 11 miles per hour or faster disperses it over 4 rounds, and a strong wind of 21 miles per hour or faster disperses it in just 1 round.

name: Binding Winds
description: You create a whirling barrier of air that encircles the target and holds it in place for as long as you concentrate. The barrier itself doesn't move; instead it becomes a physical wall surrounding the subject, so the subject can act normally but cannot move from where it's standing. The winds carry the subject's voice away, so it can speak but can't be heard, and it can't hear anything except the roar of the wind. No sonic spell or language-dependent spell or effect can be cast into or out of the binding winds, though a spell you cast on yourself still functions normally. Ranged attacks made into or out of the barrier suffer a –2 penalty. The binding winds hold a flying creature suspended in midair just as effectively as they hold a grounded one. A Reflex save negates the effect, and spell resistance applies.

name: Dance of the Unicorn
description: You surround yourself with a swirling, purifying mist, with a radius of 5 feet per caster level, for 1 minute per caster level. The mist washes the air clean of smoke, dust, and poison. Any nonmagical contaminant inside the cloud, including an inhaled poison, is automatically neutralized. A magical hazard such as acid fog, cloudkill, or a green dragon's breath is negated outright only if your caster level is higher than the effect's own caster level, or higher than the dragon's Hit Dice. If your level is lower, everyone inside the mist instead gets a +4 bonus on their saving throw against that hazard. Everything inside the cloud is left damp once the mist passes over it.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Phantom Stag
description:
You conjure a Large, corporeal, staglike creature to carry you or a person you designate into combat or across open country at great speed. The phantom stag has a black body and head, sharp silvery antlers, and smoke-colored, insubstantial hooves that make no sound as it moves. It wears no saddle, bridle, or bit, but it's exceptionally attentive to its rider's shifts in balance and nudges. The spell lasts 1 hour per caster level, and there's no saving throw or spell resistance involved.

The phantom stag has an Armor Class of 20, made up of a –1 penalty for its size, a +6 natural armor bonus, and a +5 Dexterity bonus. It has 40 hit points plus 5 hit points per caster level. It attacks with its antlers at a +10 bonus, dealing 1d8+9 points of damage, doubled if it charges. It can also trample a Medium or smaller foe as it moves through that creature's space, dealing 1d6+9 points of damage unless the foe succeeds on a Reflex save. Its speed is 20 feet per caster level, to a maximum of 300 feet. It can carry its rider's weight plus up to 10 pounds per caster level. It ignores difficult terrain such as undergrowth, rubble, or mud that would normally slow it down.

A phantom stag also gains abilities based on your caster level, and a mount created by a higher-level caster keeps every ability granted at a lower level as well. At 12th level, the stag can use air walk at will, with no action required to activate it, though it can only stay aloft for up to 1 round at a time before settling back to the ground; it also gains a +2 deflection bonus to AC. At 14th level, it gains a full flying speed with average maneuverability, and its deflection bonus rises to +4. At 16th level, its antlers gain the wounding and ghost touch weapon qualities, and its deflection bonus rises to +6. At 18th level, it can use etherealness on its rider's behalf, as the spell, and its deflection bonus rises to +8.

functionsAs.note: Referenced spell not currently in data/spells/.

name: Poison Thorns
description: Black, glistening thorns emerge painlessly from your own skin for 1 round per caster level. Any creature that grapples you, or that strikes you in melee with a handheld weapon or a natural weapon, takes 1d6 points of piercing damage plus your Strength bonus from the thorns protecting you. A weapon with exceptional reach, such as a longspear, keeps its wielder out of the thorns' range. You can't use the thorns to attack — they only punish someone who attacks you. A scratch from the thorns is also enough to deliver a dose of poison: any creature grappling you is exposed to it at the start of each of your turns. The poison deals 1d4 points of temporary Strength damage immediately, and another 1d4 points of temporary Strength damage a minute later. Each of those two instances of damage can be negated separately by a successful Fortitude save, with a DC of 10 plus half your caster level plus your Wisdom modifier. You need a dried black rose as a material component.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Quill Blast
description: Needle-sharp quills erupt from your skin and fly outward in every direction as you finish casting this spell, striking everyone within a 20-foot-radius spread centered on you. How many quills hit a given creature depends on its size. A Tiny or smaller creature that fails its save is struck by 1 quill, and a Tiny or smaller creature that succeeds avoids the quills entirely. A Small creature takes 1d4 quills. A Medium creature takes 2d6 quills. A Large creature takes 3d6 quills. A Huge or larger creature takes 4d6 quills. A creature that makes its Reflex save is struck by only half as many quills as it would otherwise take. Each quill that hits deals 1d6 points of piercing damage and lodges in the flesh of any living creature it strikes. Every quill still lodged in a creature imposes a –1 penalty on that creature's attack rolls, saving throws, and checks. A quill can be removed safely with a DC 20 Heal check, taking a standard action; removing it any other way deals an extra 1d6 points of damage. You need a porcupine quill as a material component.

name: Rejuvenation Cocoon
description: You touch a willing creature and encase it in a temporary cocoon of energy that heals it and shields it for 2 rounds. The cocoon is glowing, yellow-green, and made of force, though it's flexible enough to respond to pressure from inside. It forms a few inches out from the target's body, but it deforms enough to let the target reach into a backpack, cast a spell with a somatic component, draw a weapon, or take similar actions. The target can't move out of the space it occupies while the cocoon holds it, and it can't leave early except by using teleportation magic or by dealing enough damage to break the cocoon open. The cocoon has hardness 10 and 10 hit points per caster level; destroying it ends the spell immediately. One round after the cocoon forms, it heals the target 10 points of damage per caster level and purges it of poison and disease. At the end of the second round, the cocoon dissolves and the target emerges, free to move and act normally. A Will save negates the effect, though it's harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way. You need a butterfly's cocoon as a material component.

name: Vigor, Greater
description: This spell works exactly like lesser vigor, except it grants fast healing 4. It lasts 10 rounds plus 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 35 rounds.

name: Anger of the Noonday Sun

targetAreaEffect.value: All sighted creatures within a 10-ft.-radius burst centered on you

description: You unleash a blinding flash of sunlight that bursts outward from you to a radius of 10 feet. Any sighted creature within the burst who can see you must make a saving throw or be blinded. The blindness lasts 1 minute per caster level. An undead creature caught in the burst takes 1d6 points of damage per two caster levels, to a maximum of 10d6, or half that damage if it makes a successful Reflex save. If an undead creature is one that's specifically vulnerable to bright light, such as a vampire, and it fails its save, the light destroys it outright. The same ultraviolet light also damages fungi, molds, oozes, and slimes exactly as it would an undead creature.

name: Cometfall
description: You conjure a bright, glowing comet made of rock and ice, which appears in midair above your enemies and then plummets to the ground with tremendous force. It appears 5 feet per caster level above the ground, or at the ceiling if that's lower. As it falls, it deals 2d6 points of damage per 10 feet it drops to everything within the 10-foot-square area directly beneath it; a Reflex save halves this damage. The force of the impact can also knock creatures prone: any creature that failed its Reflex save is also subject to a trip attempt, with the comet using a +11 bonus on the check, made up of +7 for its effective Strength of 25 and +4 for being Large. When the comet strikes, it breaks apart and fills the 10-foot-square area with dense rubble.

name: Contagious Touch
description: When you cast this spell, you choose one disease from a specific list: blinding sickness, cackle fever, filth fever, mindfire, red ache, the shakes, or slimy doom. For 1 round per caster level, any living creature you hit with a melee touch attack is exposed to that disease exactly as though you'd cast contagion on it, and it contracts the disease immediately unless it succeeds on a Fortitude save. You can infect no more than one creature per round.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF), even though the spell's own touch-attack effect triggers a Fortitude save as described. Filled in as Fortitude negates/Yes here, matching the same spell's printing in both Masters of the Wild and Spell Compendium.

name: Crumble
description: You bring the forces of erosion to bear on a single fabricated object — a stone bridge, a wooden building, an iron wall, a construct, or anything else not formed by nature itself. The erosion deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level to the object, ignoring its hardness, to a maximum of 15d6. The spell has no effect on a living creature, though it does affect a construct. The maximum size of object you can affect depends on your caster level: up to Huge if you're 15th level or lower, Gargantuan if you're 16th to 18th level, and Colossal if you're 19th or 20th level. If you cast the spell on an object larger than your level allows, the spell simply fails. A Fortitude save allows the object a partial effect, and spell resistance applies to the object as normal.

name: Enveloping Cocoon

targetAreaEffect.value: Cocoon of force around one Large or smaller creature

description:
A cocoon of shimmering blue-green force closes around one Large or smaller creature, holding it inside for 1 round per caster level or until the cocoon is destroyed. The cocoon has hardness 10 and 10 hit points per caster level. While it holds, the trapped creature can't move or cast a spell with a somatic component. The cocoon is too confining to let the creature inside swing anything larger than a natural or light weapon, and even then, it can only attack the cocoon itself.

As the caster, you can attach a second spell to the cocoon by casting that spell directly at it. When the enveloping cocoon ends, whether by expiring or being dismissed, the attached spell automatically strikes the trapped creature with no saving throw allowed, though spell resistance, if the creature has any, still applies. If instead the cocoon is destroyed before the duration ends or before you dismiss it, the attached spell is wasted. You can attach any of the following spells: baleful polymorph, blight, contagion, dominate animal, flame strike, infestation of maggots, languor, miasma, or phantasmal disorientation. You can also attach poison, in which case the target is treated as having already failed its first save and only needs to attempt the second. A Reflex save negates the initial cocoon effect, and spell resistance applies to it as well. You need a live caterpillar as a material component.

name: Fires of Purity
description:
You touch a creature, and it bursts into magical flame that leaves it completely unharmed, though the flame is quite capable of harming anyone else. For 1 round per caster level, any time the subject lands a successful melee attack, it deals an extra 1d6 points of fire damage, plus 1 point per caster level to a maximum of +15; if the target of that attack has spell resistance, the resistance applies to this extra damage. If any creature strikes the subject in melee, that attacker takes the same burning damage in return, unless it's using a weapon with exceptional reach, such as a longspear.

Any creature that takes fire damage from this spell must succeed on a Reflex save or catch fire. A creature that catches fire burns for 1d4 rounds, taking 1d6 points of fire damage each round, unless it succeeds on a fresh Reflex save at the spell's DC each round or douses itself in water. The subject of the spell itself takes only half damage from any fire-based attack, and if that attack would normally allow a Reflex save for half damage, the subject takes no damage at all on a successful save. The saving throw and spell resistance entries for the subject are both harmless; anyone burned through contact with the subject resists as described above.

name: Miasma
description: You fill the subject's mouth and throat with unbreathable gas, leaving it able to do little more than cough and spit for up to 3 rounds per caster level. The subject can hold its breath for 2 rounds per point of Constitution it has. After that, it must succeed on a Constitution check every round to keep holding its breath, with the DC starting at 10 and increasing by 1 for each check it has already passed. Failing any of these checks, or choosing to breathe voluntarily, knocks the subject unconscious at 0 hit points. On the following round, it drops to –1 hit points and begins dying. On the round after that, it suffocates outright.

name: Phantasmal Disorientation
description: You create ever-shifting phantasmal terrain and landmarks that confuse the subject whenever it tries to move, for up to 10 minutes per caster level. The ground beneath the subject's feet seems to shift and twist, and the landscape appears to move on its own. Each round the subject wants to move, it must attempt a DC 20 Survival check to tell the real landmarks apart from the phantasmal ones. If it succeeds, it moves normally. If it fails, it instead moves in a direction 90 degrees off course, with an equal chance of veering left or right. Because of the illusion, the subject doesn't realize it went the wrong way until it meaningfully interacts with its surroundings, such as making an attack or opening a door, or until the round ends. If it discovers the mistake before the round is over, it can attempt a new Survival check to try moving in the right direction instead, though it won't know whether that second check succeeded until it interacts with the environment again or the round ends. The spell affects only movement — a creature under its effect can still fight, cast spells, and act normally in every other way. A Will save negates the effect, and spell resistance applies.

name: Tidal Surge

targetAreaEffect.value: One or more creatures in a 20-ft.-radius burst

description:
You create a huge wave of water that slams into one or more targets within range. If there's no large natural source of water — a river, lake, or ocean — within range of the spell, the wave can only strike a single target. If such a source does exist within range, the spell instead creates a burst of water centered on a location you designate, striking every creature within that area. Either way, the water deals 1d8 points of damage per two caster levels, to a maximum of 7d8, to whatever it strikes; a Reflex save halves this damage.

Every creature struck also suffers a bull rush attempt from the wave, forcing an opposed Strength check. The water has an effective Strength of 16 and counts as Medium size, or Strength 20 and Large size if the wave was drawn from an existing source of water. You choose the direction the wave pushes when you cast the spell. A creature that loses the opposed check is pushed back 5 feet, plus another 5 feet for every 5 points by which the wave's check beat its own, in the direction you chose — and if the wave came from a body of water, this can push a character into that water. The wave also extinguishes any torch, campfire, exposed lantern, or other open flame that's Large size or smaller, whether it's carried by a target or simply sitting in the area. If the wave strikes a magical fire, that fire is targeted by a dispel magic effect exactly as if you had cast it yourself.

name: Tortoise Shell
description: You touch a living creature and grant it the armor plating of a tortoise across its torso, along with tough, leathery skin everywhere else, for 10 minutes per caster level. The effect grants a +6 enhancement bonus to the creature's existing natural armor bonus. That enhancement bonus increases by 1 for every three caster levels you have above 11th, to a maximum of +9 at 20th level. It stacks with the target's own natural armor bonus, but it doesn't stack with any other enhancement bonus to natural armor the target might have. A creature with no natural armor at all is treated as having an effective natural armor bonus of +0, the same way a character wearing only ordinary clothing has an armor bonus of +0. Tortoise shell slows the creature's movement exactly as if it were wearing heavy armor — an elf under this spell, for example, would have a speed of 20 feet and could run at 60 feet per round. Aside from that speed penalty, the spell has no other drawback: it carries no armor check penalty and no arcane spell failure chance. Spell resistance applies to the effect, though it's harmless.

name: Vigorous Circle
description: This spell works exactly like mass lesser vigor, except it grants fast healing 3 instead of fast healing 1. It lasts 10 rounds plus 1 round per caster level, to a maximum of 40 rounds.

name: Brilliant Aura

targetAreaEffect.value: 1 person per 2 levels, all of whom must be within 30 ft. of each other

description: You wreathe your allies in a glowing nimbus that transforms their weapon attacks into brilliant energy, for 1 round per caster level. You can affect one person per two caster levels, provided all of them are within 30 feet of each other. Each affected creature gives off light like a torch, with a 20-foot radius. Every melee or ranged weapon attack that affected creature makes functions as if made with a brilliant energy weapon: it ignores nonliving matter, so armor bonuses and enhancement bonuses to AC don't count against it. Those same attacks can't harm undead, constructs, or objects, since brilliant energy weapons pass through nonliving matter entirely. Every attack an affected creature makes also gains an enhancement bonus to damage equal to half the caster's level, to a maximum of +10. A Will save negates the effect for anyone who resists it, though it's harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way.

name: Cloudwalkers

targetAreaEffect.value: One creature/level, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

description: You create gaseous pads of cloudstuff on the feet of one creature per caster level, provided no two of them are ever more than 30 feet apart, letting each of them walk on the clouds for 1 hour per caster level. Each subject can move straight up or straight down at a speed of up to 30 feet using the pads. A subject can also move laterally with a fly speed of 60 feet and perfect maneuverability, but only if that subject is already at least 90 feet off the ground. To touch the earth again, a subject must spend a standard action shaking off the cloudstuff, which ends the spell for that creature alone. You can dismiss the whole spell early, but only for every affected subject at once, which can leave anyone still in the air stranded when it happens. A Reflex save negates the effect for anyone who resists it, though it's harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way.

name: Creeping Cold, Greater
description: This spell works exactly like creeping cold, except the damage keeps building longer. It adds a fourth round to the duration, dealing 4d6 points of damage that round. If you're at least 15th level, it adds a fifth round dealing 5d6 points of damage. If you're at least 20th level, it adds a sixth round dealing 6d6 points of damage.

name: Poison Vines
description: This spell works like vine mine, except the vines you create are coated in a contact poison that deals 1d6 points of temporary Dexterity damage initially and 2d6 points of temporary Dexterity damage as a secondary effect. A creature only has to make a Fortitude save against the poison the first time it enters the spell's area, and again a minute after that — it doesn't need to save again just for staying inside or for re-entering later. You're immune to the poison of vines you create, and you can extend that same immunity to a number of other creatures equal to your caster level. Spell resistance applies to the poison.

functionsAs.note: No explicit book citation in the source text; inferred because this is the only printing of this spell in our data.

name: Slime Wave
description:
You create a wave of green slime that begins at a point you choose within range and violently spreads to fill a 15-foot-radius area, splashing onto any wall or ceiling it passes for 1 round per caster level. Green slime devours flesh and organic material on contact, and it even eats through metal. Any creature that fails a Reflex save is covered with one patch of slime for every 5 feet of its facing.

Each patch deals 1d6 points of temporary Constitution damage per round to living flesh, or 2d6 points of damage per round to wood or metal, ignoring metal's hardness but not wood's; the slime doesn't harm stone at all. On the first round of contact, a patch of slime can be scraped off, though doing so is likely to ruin whatever's used to scrape it. After the first round, the only ways to remove it are freezing, burning, or cutting it away, and each of those methods also damages the victim. Extreme cold or heat, direct sunlight, or a remove disease spell destroys the slime outright. Unlike ordinary green slime, the slime this spell creates gradually evaporates on its own, and it's completely gone by the time the spell's duration ends. You need a few drops of stagnant pond water as a material component.

name: Storm Tower
description: You form a tower of dark, swirling storm clouds, 100 feet tall with a 20-foot radius, that negates several forms of magic and ranged combat within it, for 1 round per caster level. Anyone inside the tower has any electricity damage they'd take absorbed by the storm. Magic missiles can't be cast into, out of, or within the storm tower. The tower is filled with 60-mile-per-hour winds, so ranged attacks inside it are impossible, though the winds don't otherwise affect the movement of creatures within it. Only a Gargantuan or Colossal creature can pass through the tower's outer edge; every creature of a lesser size that reaches the edge must stop there. Anyone inside the storm tower has one-half concealment relative to anyone outside it. The howling winds also impose a –10 penalty on Listen checks made within 50 feet of the tower, including checks made by anyone inside it.

name: Awaken, Mass

targetAreaEffect.value: One animal or tree/three levels, no two of which may be more than 30 ft. apart

description:
You spend 24 hours awakening one animal or tree per three caster levels to humanlike sentience, provided no two of your targets are ever more than 30 feet apart. Every creature you awaken with a single casting must be of the same kind. To succeed, you must make a Will save with a DC equal to 10 plus the Hit Dice of the highest-HD target, or the Hit Dice the highest target tree will have once it's awakened, whichever number is greater. If you fail that save, the spell fails for every target at once. Each creature you awaken becomes friendly toward you, though you gain no special empathic bond or connection with it; instead, it serves you in specific tasks or endeavors whenever you communicate what you want from it.

An awakened tree gains the same characteristics as an animated object, except its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores are each 3d6. An awakened tree also gains the ability to move its limbs, roots, vines, and other growth, along with senses similar to a human's. An awakened animal instead gains an Intelligence score of 3d6, a +1d3 bonus to its Charisma score, and 2 additional Hit Dice. An awakened tree or animal can speak one language that you know, plus one additional language you know for every point of Intelligence bonus it has, if any. Awakening a creature this way costs 250 XP per creature.

name: Phantom Wolf
description:
You spend a full round conjuring an incorporeal white wolf with abnormally large, frosty jaws. The phantom wolf follows your mental commands and acts on your behalf as long as it stays within the spell's range and you continue concentrating on it, for up to 1 round per caster level. It appears wherever you designate, and it acts as you direct on your turn. You don't need to maintain line of effect to it once it's summoned, but the spell ends the instant the phantom wolf leaves the spell's range. There's no saving throw and no spell resistance against the summoning itself.

The Phantom Wolf is a Large magical beast with the incorporeal subtype. It has 12d10+48 Hit Dice, giving it 113 hit points. Its initiative modifier is +9. Its speed is a fly speed of 60 feet with good maneuverability. Its Armor Class is 25, with the same value for touch AC and 16 for flat-footed AC. Its base attack bonus is +12. It attacks with a melee touch attack at +21, or +22 on a full attack, dealing 2d6 points of damage plus 3d6 points of cold damage from its bite. Its frightful presence forces any creature with fewer than 12 Hit Dice within 30 feet of it to succeed on a DC 24 Will save or become frightened for 3d6 rounds when the wolf attacks; a creature that succeeds on that save becomes immune to that same phantom wolf's frightful presence for the next 24 hours. Its Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saves are +12, +17, and +7. Its ability scores are Dexterity 29, Constitution 18, Intelligence 11, Wisdom 17, and Charisma 26, with no Strength score at all. Its skills include Listen +20 and Spot +20, and its feats are Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Mobility, and Weapon Focus (bite). Its incorporeal traits mean it can be harmed only by another incorporeal creature, a magic weapon, a spell, a spell-like ability, or a supernatural ability. Against any other kind of attack, it has a 50% chance to ignore the damage entirely, except for a force effect or an attack made with a ghost touch weapon. It can pass through solid objects at will, though not through force effects. Its own attacks ignore natural armor, armor, and shields, though deflection bonuses and force effects still work normally against it. It always moves in complete silence and can't be detected with a Listen check if it doesn't want to be heard.

name: Storm of Elemental Fury

targetAreaEffect.value: 40-ft.-radius storm cloud, 200 feet above the ground

description:
You spend a full round conjuring a black storm cloud that hovers 200 feet above the ground, striking your enemies below with a terrifying combination of effects drawn from the Elemental Planes. The spell lasts as long as you concentrate on it, up to a maximum of 4 rounds, and it ends the instant you stop concentrating.

The moment the storm cloud appears, it buffets the area within 40 feet directly below it with a whirling windstorm, functioning as described on pages 94–95 of the Dungeon Master's Guide. Ranged attacks are impossible anywhere in the area. A Small or smaller creature must succeed on a Fortitude save or be blown away. A Medium creature must succeed on a Fortitude save or be knocked prone. A Large or larger creature must succeed on a Fortitude save just to move that round. A flying creature that fails its save is instead blown in a random direction: 1d6×5 feet if it's Large or larger, 1d6×10 feet if it's Medium, or 2d6×10 feet if it's Small or smaller. Any spell cast within the area is disrupted unless the caster succeeds on a Concentration check, with a DC equal to the storm's own save DC plus the level of the spell being cast.

If you stop concentrating on the spell after casting it, the spell ends right away. As long as you keep concentrating, the storm generates an additional effect on each of the following rounds, occurring during your turn. As a move action on top of the standard action you spend maintaining concentration, you can also move the storm cloud up to 40 feet in any direction. On the second round, chunks of rock fall from the sky, dealing 5d6 points of bludgeoning damage with no saving throw allowed. On the third round, a deluge of rain extinguishes any unprotected flame, and has a 50% chance of extinguishing a protected one; the rain also cuts visibility to 5 feet and halves everyone's movement speed in the area. On the fourth round, flame pelts the area beneath the storm cloud, dealing 1d6 points of fire damage per caster level, halved by a successful Reflex save.

name: Stormrage
description: You harness the power of wind and storm to move, protect yourself, and attack, for 1 minute per caster level. You gain the benefits of a fly spell, and you're protected on every side as if surrounded by a wind wall. You're also completely unaffected by any natural or magical wind, such as a hurricane or a gust of wind spell, and you're entirely uninhibited by any of the usual adverse effects of extreme wind, such as needing to make Concentration checks because of strong gusts. Finally, you can discharge bolts of electricity from your own eyes. Your caster level sets the total number of d6 you can generate with this power, to a maximum of 20d6, and you can use them all in a single bolt or divide them across several rounds. For example, a 16th-level caster could fire an 8d6 bolt in one round and another 8d6 bolt the next, or fire sixteen separate 1d6 bolts over sixteen or more rounds, or combine every die into a single 16d6 bolt — and every bolt you fire this way affects only one creature. Launching a bolt is a standard action that doesn't provoke an attack of opportunity. Each bolt has a range of 100 feet and requires a ranged touch attack to hit, though you gain a +3 bonus on that attack roll if the target is wearing metal armor, is made of metal, or is carrying a significant amount of metal.
note: Complete Divine's printed entry has no Saving Throw or Spell Resistance line at all (confirmed against the source PDF) — the book omits them for this Personal/You-only spell. Filled in as None/No here, matching the same spell's printing in Spell Compendium.

name: Nature’s Avatar
description: You touch an animal and infuse it with the spirit of nature itself, for 1 minute per caster level. The animal gains a +10 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls. It also gains 1d8 temporary hit points per caster level. On top of that, it gains the full benefit of a haste effect. A Will save negates the effect for the animal if it resists, though the effect is harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way.

name: Phantom Bear
description:
This spell works exactly like phantom wolf, except you conjure an incorporeal bear with a fearsome roar instead of a wolf, under the same range and concentration limits.

The Phantom Bear is a Huge magical beast with the incorporeal subtype. It has 14d10+48 Hit Dice, giving it 113 hit points. Its initiative modifier is +9. Its speed is a fly speed of 60 feet with good maneuverability. Its Armor Class is 25, with the same value for touch AC and 16 for flat-footed AC. Its base attack bonus is +14. On a full attack, it makes two claw attacks at +23 each, dealing 2d6 points of damage plus 3d6 points of cold damage apiece, and one bite attack at +21, dealing 2d8 points of damage plus 3d6 points of cold damage. It can loose a fearsome roar once every 1d4 rounds: everyone within 120 feet of it, except you, must succeed on a DC 26 Will save or become frightened for 3d6 rounds, and anyone within 30 feet of it who fails that save becomes panicked instead of merely frightened. Its Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saves are +13, +17, and +7. Its ability scores are Dexterity 29, Constitution 20, Intelligence 11, Wisdom 17, and Charisma 28, with no Strength score at all. Its skills include Listen +20 and Spot +20, and its feats are Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Mobility, Multiattack, and Weapon Focus (bite). Its incorporeal traits are identical to the phantom wolf's: it can be harmed only by another incorporeal creature, a magic weapon, a spell, a spell-like ability, or a supernatural ability, with a 50% chance to ignore damage from any other source entirely, except for a force effect or a ghost touch weapon. It can pass through solid objects at will, though not through force effects. Its attacks ignore natural armor, armor, and shields, though deflection bonuses and force effects still work normally against it. It always moves in complete silence and can't be detected with a Listen check if it doesn't want to be heard.

name: Shadow Landscape

targetAreaEffect.value: One-mile radius spread, centered on a point in space

description:
You spend a full hour infusing the landscape around you with power stolen from the Plane of Shadow, making the surrounding terrain a more savage, dangerous place for 1 day per caster level. The spell affects a one-mile-radius area centered on a point you choose within range, and exactly what changes depends on the kind of terrain that area contains.

If the area is desert, the spell makes it a place no one goes willingly. The average temperature rises by 30 degrees, or drops by 30 degrees instead if the desert is actually a tundra. Sandstorms, or snowstorms if it's a tundra, sweep through the area on an hourly basis.

If the area is forest, the trees grow strangely twisted, and a canopy of rotting leaves blocks out the sun. Any space with light undergrowth instead has heavy undergrowth. Any space with heavy undergrowth grasps at anyone passing through it, exactly as if an entangle spell had been cast there, with a Reflex save allowed at the shadow landscape's own DC for a partial effect.

If the area is hill terrain, it grows more treacherous. Light undergrowth becomes heavy undergrowth. Slopes feel steeper than their actual elevation would suggest: climbing a gradual slope costs two squares of movement instead of one, and climbing a steep slope costs four squares. Cliffs develop frequent overhangs and crumbling rock, requiring a DC 25 Climb check to ascend or descend.

If the area is marsh, it grows swampier and more forbidding. Half of the undergrowth spaces in the marsh turn into quicksand.

If the area is mountain terrain, it becomes a place of jagged peaks, slippery slopes, and howling winds. Cliffs and chasms require a DC 25 Climb check to scale. Anyone who fails a Climb check, or who makes a loud noise, has a 10% chance of triggering an avalanche. Altitude effects also worsen by one full category: any area below 5,000 feet is treated as though it were in the 5,000-to-15,000-foot category, and anything above 5,000 feet is treated as though it were above 15,000 feet.

If the area is plains, only the area's natural grasslands are affected. They become wide-open spaces dotted with thick stands of bushes, where thunderstorms and tornadoes strike frequently. Half of the undergrowth spaces, whether light or heavy, grasp at anyone passing through them exactly the way forest's heavy undergrowth does, with the same Reflex save for a partial effect. Spell resistance applies to the spell as a whole.

name: Unyielding Roots
description:
You touch a willing creature, and thick tree roots grow from it, anchoring it to the ground and channeling life-sustaining energy into it, for 1 minute per caster level. If the creature you touch isn't in contact with the ground when you cast the spell, the spell has no effect at all.

For the duration, the rooted creature can't move from the space it occupies, and nothing can move it out of that space either — not a bull rush, not an overrun, not a magical force effect such as Bigby's forceful hand, nothing short of a massive earthquake. Any such attempt simply fails. If someone tries to overrun the rooted creature, the rooted creature must block the attempt rather than choosing to avoid it, and it automatically wins the Strength check needed to stop the overrun. It can then attempt an opposed Strength check, against the overrunning creature's Strength or Dexterity check, to knock that creature prone.

The roots also draw life energy up from the ground and feed it to the rooted creature, healing it up to 30 points of damage every round, automatically neutralizing any poison affecting it, and removing negative levels exactly as a restoration spell would. As long as the roots remain, the rooted creature gains a +4 bonus on Fortitude saves and a +4 bonus on Will saves, but it takes a –4 penalty on Reflex saves. A Fortitude save negates the effect if the creature resists it, though the effect is harmless, and spell resistance applies the same way.

functionsAs.note: Referenced spell not currently in data/spells/.

name: Whirlwind, Greater
description:
You create a tornado 20 feet in radius and up to 5 feet tall per caster level, centered anywhere within range, and you can direct it to wreak destruction as you choose, flinging your foes into the air and tearing apart nearby structures for 1 round per caster level. How the greater whirlwind affects a given creature depends on that creature's size and its distance from the twister.

A Large or smaller creature that starts its turn within 60 feet of the center of the whirlwind must succeed on a Fortitude save or be dragged 1d4×10 feet toward the center, taking 1d4 points of nonlethal damage for every 10 feet it's dragged. A Huge creature within 40 feet of the twister must succeed on a Fortitude save or be knocked prone. A Gargantuan or Colossal creature within 40 feet of the twister must succeed on a Fortitude save before it can move away from the twister at all.

A flying creature of Huge size or smaller that fails its Fortitude save is instead sucked all the way to the center of the twister, taking 2d6 points of damage from the battering and buffeting. A Gargantuan flying creature that fails its save is pulled 1d6×10 feet toward the twister's center instead. A Colossal flying creature that fails its save is pulled 1d6×5 feet toward the center.

Any creature that starts its turn inside the tornado takes 6d6 points of damage for each of 1d10 rounds it remains trapped there, rolled separately for every creature caught inside. A creature trapped inside the tornado can't do much of anything — attacking, casting spells, and moving are all impossible while it's inside. When the greater whirlwind eventually expels a creature, that creature reappears 4d6×5 feet away from the twister's center, in a random direction, and 4d6×5 feet off the ground, falling immediately if it can't fly.

The tornado automatically uproots trees and other vegetation in its path, and it leaves a trail of dense rubble wherever it goes. Any structure caught within the greater whirlwind takes 2d6 points of damage per round. Fortitude allows a partial effect against everything the spell does, and spell resistance applies throughout.
